description: Convert between markup and margin, or price a product from cost plus a target margin.

faqs.a: Markup = (price − cost) ÷ cost — profit as a share of cost. Margin = (price − cost) ÷ price — profit as a share of price. Margin is always lower than markup for the same deal.
faqs.q: Markup vs margin — what is the difference?

faqs.a: Price = cost ÷ (1 − margin%). For a $40 cost and 25% margin target: $40 ÷ 0.75 = $53.33.
faqs.q: How do I price from cost + margin?

faqs.a: Margin = markup ÷ (1 + markup). A 50% markup equals a 33.33% margin.
faqs.q: How do I convert markup to margin?

howto: Mode 1: enter cost and price to get both markup % and margin %.
Mode 2: enter cost and a target margin to get the selling price.
